lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Good morning, Central Bus Station. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I would like two tickets to Lakeside on Friday morning, please.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Buses to Lakeside leave at nine fifteen and eleven forty-five. Which time would you prefer?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: The nine fifteen, please. How much are the tickets?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: A single ticket is twelve pounds, so two tickets cost twenty-four pounds in total.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: And your bus leaves from platform three.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Oh, wait a moment. That was last week's timetable. This week, the Lakeside bus leaves from platform five.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Please arrive at the platform fifteen minutes before the bus leaves.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Platform five, fifteen minutes early. Thank you for your help.

sentences.text: Night markets are a common sight in many Asian cities, where rows of small stalls open as the sun goes down.
Most markets begin trading at about six in the evening and stay open until midnight.
Visitors come mainly for the food, which is cooked in front of them and sold more cheaply than in restaurants.
The most popular dishes are usually local specialities, such as grilled seafood or noodle soups, rather than food from other countries.
In recent years, some markets have added live music and craft stalls to attract younger visitors.
However, the growth of the markets has brought problems, including noise for nearby residents and large amounts of litter.
To deal with this, some city councils now require stall holders to use paper packaging instead of plastic.
Despite these problems, night markets remain an important part of city life, because they give small family businesses a cheap place to sell their goods.
